opex.heading: Operating Expenses
opex.text: Operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $18,444,000, an increase of $3,357,000, or 22.3%, compared to the $15,087,000 for the third quarter of 2025. For the year-to-date period ended September 30, 2026, operating expenses totaled $54,994,000, an increase of $11,667,000, or 26.9%, compared to the same period in 2025. The following tables detail the categories that comprise operating expenses.

For the year-to-date period ended September 30, 2026, operating expenses totaled $54,994,000, an increase of $11,667,000, or 26.9%, compared to the same period in 2025. The following tables detail the categories that comprise operating expenses.

prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provision for credit losses includes a provision for losses on loans, available-for-sale debt securities, and unfunded loan commitments. The provision provides for losses inherent in the financial assets as determined by a quarterly analysis and calculation of various factors related to the financial assets. The amount of the provision reflects the adjustment management determines necessary to ensure the Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) is adequate to cover any losses inherent in the financial assets.

The Corporation recorded a provision release of $374,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 consisting of a provision release related to loans of $588,000, net of a $214,000 provision for off-balance sheet credit exposure and $0 related to available for sale securities. For the three months ended September 30, 2025, the Corporation recorded a provision for credit losses of $20,000 consisting of provision related to loans of $100,000, net of a provision release for off-balance sheet losses of $80,000 and $0 related to available for sale securities. The Corporation recorded a provision release of $858,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 consisting of a provision release related to loans of $727,000, $131,000 in provision release for off-balance sheet credit exposure and $0 related to available for sale securities.

nonop.heading: Other Income
nonop.text: Other income for the third quarter of 2026 was $4,360,000, an increase of $134,000, or 3.2%, compared to the $4,226,000 earned during the third quarter of 2025. Other income for the year-to-date period was $12,801,000, an increase of $1,670,000, or 15.0% from the year-to-date period in 2025. The following tables detail the categories that comprise other income:

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Federal and state income tax expense was $1,674,000 and $1,419,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, resulting in an effective tax rate of 19.5% and 19.3%. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, income tax expense was $4,031,000 and $3,781,000 for an effective tax rate of 19.5% and 19.1%. Generally, the Corporation’s effective tax rate is less than the 21% federal statutory rate due to tax-exempt income, including interest earned on tax-exempt investment securities and loans, and income from life insurance policies, partially offset by disallowed interest expense, state income taxes, and non-deductible acquisition related expenses. The increase in the year-to-date effective rate is due to state tax expense with the acquisition of Cecil and doing business in Maryland, and non-deductible acquisition-related expenses.

net.text: The Corporation recorded net income of $6,913,000 for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, a $994,000, or 16.8% increase over the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net income for the nine-month period was $16,641,000, a $596,000, or 3.7% increase over earnings in the nine-month period ended September 30, 2025. Basic and diluted earnings per share of common stock were $1.21 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.04 for the same period in 2025, and for the year-to-date period, basic and diluted earnings per share of common stock were $2.92, compared to $2.83 in 2025, or a 3.1% increase over the comparable nine-month period in the previous year.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income (NII)
Net interest income.text:
NII represents the largest portion of the Corporation’s operating income, which consists of NII and non-interest income, and represents 81% - 84% of the total for all periods presented in 2026 and 2025. The overall performance of the Corporation is highly dependent on interest rates and the changes in NII since it comprises such a significant portion of operating income.

The following table shows a summary analysis of NII on a fully taxable equivalent (FTE) basis. For analytical purposes and throughout this discussion, yields, rates, and measurements such as NII, net interest spread, and net yield on interest earning assets are presented on an FTE basis, assuming a 21% tax rate. The FTE NII shown in both tables below will exceed the NII reported on the consolidated statements of income which is not presented on an FTE basis. The amount of FTE adjustment totaled $145,000 and $431,000 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $104,000 and $301,000 for the same periods in 2025.

intro.text: ENB Financial Corp (“the Corporation”) is a bank holding company that was formed on July 1, 2008. The Corporation’s wholly owned subsidiary, Ephrata National Bank (“the Bank”), also referred to as ENB, is a full-service commercial bank organized under the laws of the United States. Presently, no other subsidiaries exist under the bank holding company. The Bank has one subsidiary, ENB Insurance, which is a full-service insurance agency that offers a broad range of insurance products to commercial and personal clients. The Corporation and the Bank are both headquartered in Ephrata, Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. The Bank was incorporated on April 11, 1881, pursuant to The National Bank Act under a charter granted by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC).
